::: {.callout-note .part-overview icon=false}
## Why this part comes here

Human judgment is culturally accumulated and socially regulated. This part separates learning from others, conformity and norms, and specific influence triggers.
:::

## Guiding questions

- When are other people good evidence?
- How do norms and unanimity change what is speakable?
- When does a useful social signal become a counterfeit trigger?

## Chapters

- **Chapter 22:** [Social Learning, Mimicry, and Attribution](../chapters/22-social-learning-mimicry-and-attribution.qmd) — How other people become models, mirrors, and causal explanations — About 10 min
- **Chapter 23:** [Conformity, Norms, and Social Proof](../chapters/23-conformity-norms-and-social-proof.qmd) — How groups define what feels true, normal, safe, and desirable — About 8 min
- **Chapter 24:** [Authority, Bystanders, and Influence Triggers](../chapters/24-authority-bystanders-and-influence-triggers.qmd) — Signals that coordinate behavior—and can be counterfeited — About 15 min
